title: Müller wins Norisring Race 2 on pit strategy to give Audi a weekend double
dek: Nico Müller won Race 2 at the Norisring from third on the grid by 0.670 seconds, staying out longest for his stop to jump pole-sitter Blomqvist, and Wittmann retook the championship lead.

chapters.title: Audi’s breakthrough, Mercedes’ wounds
text: Saturday had rewritten the weekend. Edoardo Mortara won Race 1 for Audi, the make’s first victory at the Norisring since 2002, and went to the top of the championship on 69 points, two clear of Marco Wittmann, after Mattias Ekström’s collision took Robert Wickens out and spun Christian Vietoris from the lead. Mercedes, whose unbeaten run at the Norisring had ended on Saturday, needed an answer on Sunday. The second race ran for a full hour rather than 40 minutes, and the stewards had a decision to make on Ekström.

chapters.title: Ekström fastest, Blomqvist on pole
text: Sunday’s qualifying was run in light drizzle. It did not change the state of the track, as Nico Müller put it, but it made it harder to see through the windscreen at the limit through the Schöller-S. Paul di Resta had topped the morning’s third practice session and held the best time for a long time in qualifying.

Ekström, though, set the fastest lap, a 47.804, only for the stewards to move him back three places for the Race 1 collision. He lined up fourth. That promoted Tom Blomqvist, 0.016 seconds slower, to pole in the RBM BMW, the first of his DTM career, after a Saturday on which the team had struggled and he had started 20th. Blomqvist said they had changed the car’s set-up overnight. Di Resta was alongside him, 0.073 off the time, and Müller moved up to third, 0.085 off, with Ekström, Lucas Auer, Maxime Martin and Wickens next.

Adrien Tambay, Mortara and Wittmann completed the top ten. Vietoris, Saturday’s pole-sitter, was only 15th and Jamie Green 16th. Gary Paffett had touched the wall shortly before the midpoint of the session, damaging his suspension, and started from the back of the grid.

chapters.title: Ekström runs into di Resta at the first corner
text: Blomqvist made a good start and led into the Grundig hairpin. Müller passed di Resta on the opening lap, and Ekström, starting from fourth, went into the back of the Mercedes at the first corner. He said his front wheel locked under braking and the cars ahead of him were slow, and the contact broke the radiator on the Audi: he parked it at the end of the first lap after a weekend he called one to forget. Augusto Farfus’ MTEK BMW was also out after the opening lap.

Di Resta carried the damage through the race, losing downforce at the rear. Up front Blomqvist led, with Müller within a second of the BMW through the opening part of the race and Auer’s Mücke Mercedes, fifth on the grid, following di Resta.

chapters.title: Müller stays out longest
text: The stops decided the race. Di Resta and Martin came in early, which freed Auer to run third and set a string of fastest laps on the leaders. He pitted just as he got within range, however, and his left-rear wheel was slow to go on, a stop that dropped him behind both di Resta and Martin.

Blomqvist stopped around the half-distance mark with Müller on his tail. The Audi driver stayed out for several more laps, making use of the clear track, and then came in for a quick stop and rejoined narrowly ahead of the BMW to take the lead. Blomqvist said he had lost time at his own stop but that Müller had been quicker anyway. Müller pulled out a lead of about two seconds, and the pair ran first and second.

chapters.title: A late neutralisation wipes out the gap
text: Behind the leaders the closing stages were messy. Vietoris turned da Costa’s Schnitzer BMW around and was given a drive-through penalty, which dropped him to 15th at the flag. Wickens had a puncture and an extra stop, and Paffett, who had fought his way up from last on the grid, retired. With a few minutes left, an incident scattered debris and the safety car came out, erasing Müller’s lead.

Müller handled the restart well, taking a good jump on Blomqvist, and nothing behind him was close enough to interfere. The other front-runners behaved. In the last lap Phoenix team-mates Mike Rockenfeller and Timo Scheider touched, with Scheider finishing 16th and Rockenfeller a retirement.

chapters.title: Müller holds Blomqvist by 0.670 seconds
text: Müller won by 0.670 seconds in 1:01:03.139, his first DTM victory and Audi’s second of the weekend. He was the seventh different winner in eight races of 2016. Blomqvist was second, and Martin, from sixth on the grid, completed the podium 1.543 seconds behind, so that the RBM BMWs took both of the places behind the winner. Blomqvist also set the fastest lap, a 48.328 on lap 54.

Di Resta finished fourth with his damaged Mercedes, 4.701 seconds behind, with Auer fifth and Wittmann sixth, which was enough to put him back at the top of the standings. Spengler was seventh and Mortara eighth, and Glock and Tomczyk, who had started from the back rows, took the last two points in ninth and tenth. Wickens was 11th, Götz 12th, Ocon 13th, Molina 14th, and Green was classified 17th, 14 laps down. Seven cars retired in all.

chapters.title: Wittmann back in front by two points
text: Müller thanked his team for a perfect pit stop and the right strategy. He said Mortara had ended Audi’s 14-year wait on Saturday and that it had been his turn on Sunday, adding that standing on top of the podium was addictive. A weekend that began with Mercedes expecting to extend its run at the Norisring ended without a win for the marque, while Ekström, who lost his pole to the penalty and parked after one lap, called it a weekend to forget.

For BMW the weekend turned around. Blomqvist said Saturday had been poor but the team changed the car overnight and took it to the front row, and that it had not expected such a result before the weekend. Martin said he had used every chance from sixth on the grid and had not expected to be on the podium. Wittmann, sixth on his home track, was one of four BMWs in the top seven.

For Mercedes, di Resta said the contact with Ekström had cost him a lot of downforce at the rear and he had fought the damaged car all race. Mercedes DTM boss Ulrich Fritz said it was not the weekend the team had hoped for, since the first-lap damage had ended di Resta’s chance of fighting for the podium. Wickens left in 11th after his puncture.

Wittmann left Nuremberg on 75 points, two clear of Mortara on 73, with di Resta third on 70, Green on 63, Martin on 62 and Wickens on 58. The top three were within five points of one another, with ten of the season’s 18 races still to run. About 123,500 spectators attended over the weekend. The DTM moves to Zandvoort on 15–17 July.

facts.t: A first DTM win for Müller
facts.v: Nico Müller won in 1:01:03.139, 0.670 seconds clear of Blomqvist, and became the seventh different winner in the first eight races of 2016.

one.label: Autosport: Norisring DTM: Nico Muller beats Tom Blomqvist and gets first win

facts.v: Ekström set the fastest qualifying lap, 47.804, but a three-place grid penalty for the Race 1 collision put him fourth and gave pole to Blomqvist.
Müller stayed out until the end of the pit-stop window, then used a quick stop and quick in-laps to rejoin ahead of Blomqvist.

one.label: Autosport: Norisring DTM: Nico Muller beats Tom Blomqvist and gets first win

facts.v: A safety car with a few minutes left erased Müller’s lead of about two seconds, but he made a good restart and kept the win.

one.label: Motorsport.com: Norisring DTM: Muller beats Blomqvist for second Audi win

facts.v: Wittmann’s sixth place put him on 75 points, two clear of Mortara, and the top three drivers were separated by five points.
